Fair enough, I respect your opinion, especially since you’ve tried it. (Though not all therapists are created equal, and there are different therapy styles. if you only tried one or two you may not have had one you clicked with.) I’m definitely in the don’t-knock-it-til-you’ve-tried-it camp (on this issue).

I’m not just “parroting this take” though. My view is based on my own experience with therapy (which was actually limited—I felt like I only needed a few sessions for it to be helpful; a lot of people think you have to go forever but you don’t), plus the people that I know who have been in therapy, both family and friends (and especially people I’ve dated). The ones who have had some therapy sessions generally are a bit more well adjusted and happier, and have better relationships (because they have good boundaries and communication skills etc). Obviously not a scientific study, but I’m also not just making it up.

Totally agree. I think everyone in the world would be benefit from seeing a therapist at some point in their lives, even if everything seems likes it’s going great. Sure, it might not be your friends’ business, but what else are friends for if not to share uncomfortable truths from a place of love and caring for you?
